Sitting under the shade of the tree, he watched the sun rise for the first time. Really watched. Observed. The breaking hues of orange and pink cast purple tones under the scattered clouds. Rays of light spilled out from behind the wooded hedge, peeking just behind the rolling hills. The birds chirped their twittering songs. Waking from their slumber, the area sprang to life.

 

Contemplative, he looked behind him. He turned his head back to the glorious sight and wrapped his thin jacket around him. He didn't realize how chilly the night was. Now, lightly covered in sweat and stationary, he felt the crisp air now more than ever.

 

No use going back. Nothing's back there. Nothing I love. Nothing I care about. Maybe there's something out there. Something good. I need this.

 

He stood up, lightly dusting off the bark and dirt from his pants and coat. He took a long, shaking breath. Fear gripped him for a brief moment. His heart pounded in his chest. He could hear it -- thud. thud. thud. His legs felt weak. With trembling hands, he leaned on the slightly knotted walking stick his grandfather had given him. It dug slightly into the soft earth. He zoned out for a moment. Gazing behind him, he contemplated going back. Shaking his head, he stood up.

 

No. That's not who I want to be. Not anymore.

 

He dropped his stick for a moment, placing his hands behind his head. He closed his eyes and breathed.

 

One. two. Three. Four. Five. Six. Seven. Eight. Breathe. One. Two. Three. For. Five. Six. Seven. Eight. Breathe.

 

As his breathing returned to normal, he picked up his grandfather's walking stick. Still shaking a little, he nodded to himself. He grabbed his pack and swung it over his back.

 

Now or never.

 

Lacking confidence in his choice, he took his first step. Adjusting his cap, he proceeded to walk. His first steps as a new man were small, but as his confidence grew, he took larger ones - slow, calm, and serene. The earth under his worn boots vibrated, full of energy. He smiled. He knew his choice was the right one.
